The result is a tuple containing a tuple of one SMILES: 'Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)O)cc2)cc1'. That's the precursor? It seems the amide carbonyl turned into carboxylic acid (C(=O)O) while the amine part is missing? Actually the original amide was C(=O)N attached to an aniline (Nc3ccccc3N). The result shows C(=O)O but the amine part is gone; maybe the template only breaks the amide to acid and leaves the amine attached to something else? The result only gives one fragment, maybe the other fragment is implicit (the amine). The tool returns list of outcomes; each outcome is a tuple of precursor SMILES? It gave (('Cc1ccc(...C(=O)O)cc1',),). That's only one precursor; maybe the other is the amine fragment which is the amine part of the original amide: Nc3ccccc3N? Actually the amide nitrogen is attached to aromatic amine (c3ccccc3N). The template may produce the acid fragment and the amine fragment as separate molecules. But result only shows one. Possibly the other fragment is the amine (the N attached to phenyl). Could be missing due to representation; maybe the amine is part of the same SMILES? Let's examine: original SMILES: .../C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N. The amide nitrogen attached to phenyl with an NH2 substituent. After breaking, we get carboxylic acid fragment: .../C(=O)O (the acid). The amine fragment would be Nc3ccccc3N (an aniline with an amine). That is a separate molecule: "Nc1ccccc1N"? Actually the amine is an aniline with an extra NH2? The SMILES for that fragment: "Nc3ccccc3N" is an aniline with an amino group at para? Actually it's an aniline with an NH attached to carbonyl originally, now free amine: "Nc3ccccc3N" is an aniline with an NH attached to aromatic carbon and also an NH2 substituent? The SMILES "Nc3ccccc3N" means an aniline where the nitrogen is attached to the aromatic carbon (position 1) and also there is an N at the end? Actually "Nc3ccccc3N" is a phenyl ring with an N attached at position 1 (as substituent) and also an N attached at position? The trailing N is attached to the ring as substituent at position? The SMILES "Nc1ccccc1N" is p-phenylenediamine (two amino groups). So the amine fragment is p-phenylenediamine.

Thus the precursors are: acid fragment: "Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)O)cc2)cc1" and amine fragment: "Nc1ccccc1N". Need to verify if the amine fragment is indeed produced. The tool output didn't include it; maybe the tuple contains only one because the other is considered leaving group? But we can assume the missing fragment is the amine.

We should verify by checking if the amine fragment is present in the original molecule: yes.

Thus the possible precursor combination is [acid, amine]. Return list of lists: [["Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)O)cc2)cc1", "Nc1ccccc1N"]].
